title: Review of c09 active-gel comets c1 (SIME): replicates on fresh seeds 6 and 7: comets from noise swim 7.9-8.7 body lengths and all die within 10 time units of the substrate fork while the fed twins keep theirs; Supported
summary: I looked at the claim's sheet, tracks and starve_counts.txt, then re-ran world.py and world_starve.py (substrate removed at t=120) with labkit on new seeds 6 and 7 (200 frames, T=200). Fed: from white noise many contractile peaks form by t~8, most starve, and isolated comets (head plus regulator tail, size ~4.5 px) persist to the end; 31 tracks move >= 1 body length, the best 8.7 (seed 6, track 91) and 7.9 (seed 7, track 89). Fork: component counts at t=100/120/125/130/200 are fed 7/7/7/7/9 vs starved 7/7/6/0/0 on seed 6, and fed 7/8/8/8/9 vs starved 7/8/3/0/0 on seed 7 (counts.txt).

observations.S: rerun_fed/seed6/sheet.png t=0: white noise over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun_fed/seed6/tracks.png: tracks #89, #91, #93, #94 persist t~30-200 as single comets of constant size
observations.M: rerun_fed/seed6/FACTS.md: best track 8.7 body lengths, 31 tracks >= 1 BL; seed 7: 7.9
observations.E: counts.txt: at the t=120 fork all comets are gone by t=130 on both seeds (7->0, 8->0) while the fed twins keep 7 and 8

controls_run.E: rerun_starve/seed6, rerun_starve/seed7 (substrate removed at t=120) against the fed twins rerun_fed/seed6-7

verdicts.limitation: The comets are tiny (about 4.5 px across, area ~20 px), so their structure is close to the grid; the author's 1.5x resolution and dt/2 runs cover this, I did not repeat them. Dependence on the substrate is close to built in (the generator is made autocatalytically from s and decays), so E counts for the rung and belongs under mechanism. Runs are short (T=200, comets live ~170 time units). I did not rerun zeta=0.
